title: Biology of Viruses and Viral Diseases

questions.question: For each of the following viruses, state whether it is a DNA or RNA virus, whether it is enveloped or non-enveloped, and name an antiviral used for treatment (not immunotherapy): measles, mumps, Epstein-Barr virus, Zika, Ebola, influenza, hepatitis B, coronavirus.
questions.question_raw: AM 16. List of viruses - name whether it is DNA/RNA, Enveloped/not, and name an antiviral used for treatment (not immunotherapy) (whole chart - 3): Measles, Mumps, EBV, Zika, Ebola, Influenza, Hepatitis B (and Coronavirus)
questions.model_answer: a) Measles: ssRNA, negative-sense (Paramyxoviridae); enveloped; no specific antiviral (vitamin A supportive; ribavirin only anecdotal in severe/immunocompromised disease). Mumps: ssRNA, negative-sense (Paramyxoviridae); enveloped; no specific antiviral - supportive care. Epstein-Barr virus: dsDNA (Herpesviridae); enveloped; no proven antiviral (herpesvirus DNA-polymerase inhibitors such as acyclovir/ganciclovir reduce shedding but not disease). Zika: ssRNA, positive-sense (Flaviviridae); enveloped; no specific antiviral - supportive care. Ebola: ssRNA, negative-sense (Filoviridae); enveloped; no small-molecule antiviral of proven benefit (remdesivir studied; licensed agents are monoclonal antibodies, i.e., immunotherapy). Influenza: segmented ssRNA, negative-sense (Orthomyxoviridae); enveloped; neuraminidase inhibitors - oseltamivir, zanamivir, peramivir (or baloxavir). Hepatitis B: partially double-stranded circular DNA (Hepadnaviridae); enveloped; nucleos(t)ide polymerase inhibitors - entecavir, tenofovir (or interferon-alfa). Coronavirus: ssRNA, positive-sense; enveloped with club-shaped spikes; remdesivir/nirmatrelvir-ritonavir for SARS-CoV-2.
questions.beyond_mandell: Baloxavir and SARS-CoV-2-specific agents (remdesivir, nirmatrelvir-ritonavir) postdate/lie outside this chapter; per IDSA influenza 2018 and IDSA COVID-19 guidance.

cohort_answer.text: Measles - Paramyxoviridae, ssRNA(-), enveloped: nothing (ribavirin trialed in severe cases, vitamin A). Mumps - Paramyxoviridae, ssRNA(-), enveloped: nothing. EBV - Herpesviridae, dsDNA, enveloped: nothing (GCV, cidofovir tried). Zika - Flaviviridae, ssRNA(+), enveloped: nothing. Ebola - Filovirus, ssRNA(-), enveloped: remdesivir, or Ervebo vaccine. Influenza - Orthomyxoviridae, ssRNA(-), enveloped: Oseltamivir/zanamivir/baloxavir. Hepatitis B - Hepadnaviridae, partially ds/partly ss circular DNA, enveloped: tenofovir, lamivudine, entecavir. Chikungunya - Togaviridae, ssRNA(+), enveloped: no Rx. Coronavirus - positive sense ssRNA, enveloped with club-shaped spikes.

parts_raw.text: Fill in the table: Nucleic Acid, Envelope, and Antiviral for Mumps, Measles, Hep B, EBV, Ebola, Zika, Rotavirus, Bocavirus, Parvovirus.

questions.model_answer: a) Mumps: ssRNA, negative-sense; enveloped; none - supportive care. Measles: ssRNA, negative-sense; enveloped; none - supportive care plus vitamin A (200,000 IU PO daily x 2 days in children). Hepatitis B: partially double-stranded circular DNA; enveloped; entecavir or tenofovir (interferon-alfa an alternative). Epstein-Barr virus: dsDNA; enveloped; no antiviral of proven clinical benefit. Ebola: ssRNA, negative-sense (filovirus); enveloped; supportive care (no licensed small-molecule antiviral). Zika: ssRNA, positive-sense (flavivirus); enveloped; supportive care. Rotavirus: segmented dsRNA; non-enveloped; none - oral rehydration (zinc where deficiency is prevalent). Bocavirus: ssDNA (parvovirus family); non-enveloped; none - supportive care. Parvovirus B19: ssDNA; non-enveloped; none - supportive care (IVIG in chronic infection with pure red cell aplasia is immunotherapy, not an antiviral).
questions.cohort_conflict: Cohort calls hepatitis B a double-stranded DNA virus; it is a partially double-stranded (relaxed circular) DNA virus, and ganciclovir is not established therapy for EBV.

cohort_answer.text:
Mumps | Single-stranded, negative sense RNA | Enveloped | None - supportive care
Measles | Single-stranded, negative sense RNA | Enveloped | Vitamin A 200 000 IU PO daily x 2 days in children with suspected Vit A deficiency; Supportive care
Hep B | Double-stranded DNA virus | Enveloped | Tenofovir, Lamivudine, Entecavir
EBV | Double stranded DNA virus | Enveloped | Ganciclovir (Ian - meh)
Ebola | Single-stranded, negative sense RNA | Enveloped | Supportive care
Zika | Single-stranded, positive sense RNA | Enveloped | Supportive care
Rotavirus | Double-stranded RNA | Nonenveloped | Oral rehydration therapy, zinc supplementation in zinc deficient areas
Bocavirus | Single-stranded DNA | Nonenveloped | Supportive care
Parvovirus | Single-stranded DNA | Nonenveloped | Supportive care

questions.question: Human oncogenic viruses.
questions.model_answer: a) (1) Epstein-Barr virus - Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin disease, large B-cell lymphoma, leiomyosarcoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, multicentric Castleman disease. (2) Hepatitis B virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (3) Hepatitis C virus - hepatocellular carcinoma. (4) Human papillomavirus - cervical, anogenital and esophageal neoplasms. (5) Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (HHV-8) - Kaposi sarcoma and primary effusion lymphoma. (6) Merkel cell polyomavirus - Merkel cell carcinoma. (7) Human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 - adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

cohort_answer.text: EBV (lymphoma, nasopharyngeal CA). HTLV-1 (adult T cell lymphoma). HCV (HCC). HBV (HCC). HHV-8 (KS, primary effusion lymphoma, Castleman). HPV (cervical, penile, anal CA). Merkel Cell Polyomavirus (Merkel cell carcinoma)

questions.question: Viruses associated with pancytopenia.

parts.text: Name five viruses associated with pancytopenia

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Cytomegalovirus - direct infection of marrow stromal/progenitor cells. (2) Epstein-Barr virus - marrow suppression and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. (3) HIV - marrow suppression and dysplasia. (4) Parvovirus B19 - infects erythroid progenitors via the erythrocyte P antigen (globoside); marrow failure. (5) Hepatitis viruses (B or C) - post-hepatitis aplastic anemia/marrow suppression.
questions.beyond_mandell: Only parvovirus B19 tropism for erythroid progenitors is stated in this chapter; the pancytopenia list rests on standard Mandell disease-specific chapters.

cohort_answer.text: CMV - destroy progenitor cells. EBV - splenomegaly and marrow suppression. HIV - marrow suppression. Parvovirus - destroy progenitor cells. HBV - marrow suppression. HCV - marrow suppression

questions.question: For each of the following six viruses with malignant potential, give the associated malignancy: HHV-8, Epstein-Barr virus, human papillomavirus, HIV, hepatitis B/hepatitis C, HTLV-1.

parts.text: Fill in the associated malignancy for each virus listed.

parts_raw.text: Fill in the associated malignancy for each virus listed.

questions.model_answer: a) HHV-8 (Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus): Kaposi sarcoma and primary effusion lymphoma (also multicentric Castleman disease). Epstein-Barr virus: Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin disease, large B-cell lymphoma, leiomyosarcoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, multicentric Castleman disease (also gastric carcinoma). Human papillomavirus: cervical cancer plus other anogenital, oropharyngeal and esophageal neoplasms. HIV: no direct oncogene - immunosuppression permits AIDS-defining cancers, notably primary CNS lymphoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma and Kaposi sarcoma. Hepatitis B/hepatitis C: hepatocellular carcinoma. HTLV-1: adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma.

cohort_answer.text: HHV-8 | Kaposi's sarcoma. EBV | Burkitt's Lymphoma, gastric cancer. HPV | Cervical cancer. HIV | CNS lymphoma. HepB/HepC | HCC. HTLV-1 | Leukemia/Lymphoma.
